title: The Third Ledger
premise: Cyrus Villalobos, an estate lawyer with an unspoken gift for reading the lies people leave in paperwork, is hired to probate a will for a man still listed as alive — and the document references a 'third ledger' recording debts paid in blood. Twin letters arrive at her office: one signed confession to a death the police closed years ago, and one promising a fourth. Following the ledger's entries, Cyrus discovers the confessed killer is protecting a witness everyone believes dead — a woman who faked her drowning to escape the same circle of men, now hiding in plain sight. The final entry names the man orchestrating the deaths: the beloved judge who once saved Cyrus's own life. In the climax, Cyrus chooses justice outside the law, letting the witness vanish with the ledger while engineering the judge's exposure — and quietly burning her own name from its pages.
about_author: Bram Eriksen spent eleven years as a probate clerk in a coastal city before trading the filing room for fiction, a history that seeps into his obsession with documents that outlive their owners. He writes at night, claiming the dead are more honest after dark.

chapters.title: The Will That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Cyrus Villalobos is retained to probate the estate of Edmund Hale, who — according to every record — is alive. POV: Cyrus. The beat is quiet unease: her professional instincts itch at a document too clean, too rehearsed, and a client who flinches at the word 'ledger.'

chapters.title: Twin Letters
chapters.summary: Two envelopes arrive the same morning: a signed confession to the 2016 drowning of Marisol Quade, and a typed note promising a fourth death by month's end. POV: Cyrus. The beat is cold dread sharpening into the old hunger — the one that solved three 'accidents' the police never reopened.

chapters.title: What the Police Called an Accident
chapters.summary: Cyrus visits retired detective Ansel Roque, who closed the Quade case and owes her a debt from her third investigation. POV: Cyrus. He warns her the letters fit a pattern from a case that got a detective demoted; the beat is a door opening onto a larger, older crime.

chapters.title: The First Entry
chapters.summary: In Hale's sealed effects, Cyrus finds the ledger's first page: names, dates, and sums — payments made after deaths. POV: alternating Cyrus and an unnamed second-person voice that will later be revealed. The beat is vertigo; the ledger reads like a confession written by an accountant.

chapters.title: The Drowned Woman
chapters.summary: Cyrus tracks Marisol Quade's surviving sister, who insists Marisol couldn't swim — and shows her a photo of a woman at a funeral two years after the drowning. POV: Cyrus. The beat is the first hard proof: the confessed victim may be alive, and the confession may be armor, not guilt.

chapters.title: Hale's Silence
chapters.summary: Cyrus confronts her client about the will's impossibilities; he admits he's been paying someone for years and doesn't know who holds the ledger now. POV: Cyrus. The beat is pity curdling into fear as she realizes her client is a debtor, not a principal — and debtors start dying.

chapters.title: A Fourth Name
chapters.summary: A second letter arrives with a date and a name: Hale. POV: the unnamed second-person voice, describing surveillance of Cyrus's office. The beat is menace from inside the story's blind spot, letting the reader know someone is watching her work.

chapters.title: The Judge Who Saved Her
chapters.summary: Cyrus researches the ledger's recurring beneficiary and finds Judge Aurelio Vance — the man whose intervention kept her out of prison at twenty-three. POV: Cyrus. The beat is the book's moral fault line cracking open: her savior's name is written in the same ink as the deaths.

chapters.title: Nine Days
chapters.summary: Cyrus and Roque map the ledger's timeline and realize each entry precedes a death by exactly nine days. Hale's letter arrived six days ago. POV: Cyrus. The beat is the clock starting — the mystery becomes a countdown, and she can't go to police without exposing the witness.

chapters.title: The Woman at the Tide Line
chapters.summary: Following funeral-photo leads to a coastal town, Cyrus finds a librarian named Ana Reyes with Marisol's eyes. POV: Cyrus. The beat is a charged, wary meeting: Ana neither confirms nor denies, but slips a library slip into Cyrus's coat — a call number that matches the ledger's citation style.

chapters.title: What Survival Cost
chapters.summary: Ana's chapter: eight years ago she watched four men drown a witness and chose to become a ghost, and the ledger's keeper has been her only protection — until the letters. POV: Ana. The beat is grief and guilt; she confesses the fourth death was meant to be hers, and someone else is spending her name.

chapters.title: The Confessor
chapters.summary: Cyrus traces the confession's signature to Tomas Iriarte, a dying ex-cop who admits he wrote it — not to confess, but to force the ledger's keeper to act before he could silence Ana. POV: Cyrus visiting Iriarte. The beat is a dying man's desperate chess, and the reveal that the letters are a rescue attempt disguised as a threat.

chapters.title: Entry Seven
chapters.summary: Ledger entry seven names a man Cyrus knows: Roque's demoted partner, dead three years. She realizes Roque has been feeding her the case for his own reckoning. POV: Cyrus. The beat is betrayal's sting — everyone helping her has a debt in the book, and she may be the instrument of someone else's justice.

chapters.title: The Keeper
chapters.summary: Iriarte dies the night before Cyrus can return, his records burned — except the ledger's duplicate, mailed to her office hours after his death. POV: the second-person voice, revealed in final lines as the keeper watching her receive it. The beat is the trap closing: she was never investigating; she was being chosen.

chapters.title: Vance's Chambers
chapters.summary: Cyrus accepts a private meeting with Judge Vance, who speaks in rulings and precedents and never quite denies anything. POV: Cyrus. The beat is a duel of courtesies; she leaves certain he's the keeper's principal, and certain he knows she knows — the politest threat she's ever survived.

chapters.title: Hale's Last Entry
chapters.summary: Hale is found dead, staged as a heart attack, on day nine exactly. POV: Cyrus at the scene. The beat is fury and failure; the ledger's arithmetic is proven in blood, and Cyrus understands she has three days before the final entry — hers or Ana's.

chapters.title: The Third Copy
chapters.summary: Ana surfaces, and the two women compare ledgers: the keeper's copy, Iriarte's duplicate, and the original Ana has guarded for eight years. The originals differ. POV: Ana and Cyrus. The beat is alliance forged in mutual damage — and the discovery that the third ledger was written in two hands.

chapters.title: The Hand She Knows
chapters.summary: Cyrus matches the second handwriting to Vance's old case notes and confronts the truth: the keeper is Vance's clerk, a man Vance saved the way he once saved her — a mirror of her own path. POV: Cyrus. The beat is horrified recognition; the price of survival is the story's theme made flesh.

chapters.title: Day Nine, Again
chapters.summary: The clerk takes Ana, leaving Cyrus a final entry with a blank name and a choice: deliver the original ledger to Vance and the witness dies, or expose everything and burn with her. POV: Cyrus. The beat is the darkest hour — every legal tool she owns is useless, and the law itself is the crime scene.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Cannot Hold
chapters.summary: Cyrus walks into Vance's chambers with the original ledger and a recording, forcing his confession on the record before his own security — loyal to the law, not the man — takes him. The clerk is arrested; the fourth entry dies unfulfilled. POV: Cyrus. The beat is the climax: justice achieved by weaponizing the very system that failed everyone else.

chapters.title: The Page She Burns
chapters.summary: In the ledger's final pages, Cyrus finds her own name — a debt Vance recorded the night he saved her. She burns the page, then the copy, keeping only enough evidence to bury Vance. POV: Cyrus. The beat is the price of survival paid in full; she frees herself by choosing what to remember.

chapters.title: Ana, Alive
chapters.summary: Weeks later, a new will arrives at Cyrus's desk — drawn up for a client named Ana Reyes, witnessed by no one, referencing a fourth ledger that will never exist. POV: Cyrus. The beat is quiet, earned hope: the witness is legally alive, the dead are avenged, and Cyrus has learned which debts are worth carrying.
